extracted.intended_audience: USPTO management, OMB/congressional appropriators, auditors, and public stakeholders interested in USPTO financial and compliance practices
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, policies, metrics, and procedures the USPTO uses to manage financial reporting, fee recognition, reserves, IT/security compliance, vendor payments, and related operational metrics for patent and trademark operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: FISMA compliance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO systems achieved a 100% FISMA compliance reporting level for FY 2021, with no deficiencies that are considered to be the result of any material weaknesses in internal control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO met OMB reporting requirements, maintained continuous monitoring, coordinated with the OIG, and used this compliance posture to support year-end reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Security Impact Analysis into SDLC
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrated artifacts to support the Security Impact Analysis within the systems development life cycle that allow for the assessment of testing requirements for systems undergoing new developments, enhancements, or maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proactive approach assesses changes during development or updates and has successfully enabled security compliance; management reviews annual assessments with the OIG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper payments risk assessment (OMB A-123, Appendix C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess improper payment risks for all programs and activities, updated annually, including assessments of the control and procurement environments, as required by OMB Circular A-123, Appendix C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain internal control procedures to monitor disbursement of federal funds for valid obligations; detailed assessments and mitigation approaches are documented (see Other Information section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt Payment Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on efforts to make timely payments to vendors and on the amount of interest penalties paid for late payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics for FY2021: 99.1% of 5,808 vendor invoices processed without interest penalties; USPTO paid $14.9k in total interest penalties (~$17 per $1M disbursed). Use electronic funds transfer and Vendor Portal to improve timeliness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt Collection Improvement Act standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to standards for administrative collection, compromise, suspension, and termination of federal agency collection actions and referral for litigation; transfer debt more than 120 days old to the U.S. Department of the Treasury for cross-servicing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although minimal delinquent debt reduces material effect on USPTO, all qualifying delinquent debt is transferred for cross-servicing as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: DATA Act compliance and data standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Report financial, spending, and award data in accordance with DATA Act requirements and data standards established by the Department of the Treasury and OMB; house required data in a single source system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include extracting, validating, and reconciling data prior to submission to Treasury so that spending data displayed on USAspending.gov is consistent, reliable, accurate, and searchable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial management systems strategy (cloud migration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Realign IT into product lines and move financial management product components to public cloud software-as-a-service models where available and cost‑beneficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enterprise Business Product Line includes Financial Management, Fee Management, Planning/Budgeting/Governance, and Data & Analytics products; use of COTS components (Momentum, Aeon, Concur, Hyperion, Oracle APEX, Alteryx, Cost Perform) and cloud migration aimed at cost savings, resiliency, improved reliability, stronger cybersecurity, and enhanced user experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain distinct patent and trademark operating reserves (35 U.S.C. §42(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and track two distinct operating reserve balances—one for Patents operations and one for Trademarks operations—as required by 35 U.S.C. §42(c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating reserves are carry-over balances available without further congressional appropriation and are used to level daily differences between fee collections and costs, mitigate demand uncertainty, and finance operations during continuing resolutions or other funding timing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating reserve minimums and target levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain minimum planning reserve levels: patent operating reserve minimum $300 million and trademark operating reserve minimum $75 million (maintained above these levels for FY2020 and FY2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO plans disciplined, measured growth of the patent reserve toward an optimal level able to finance three months of operations; trademark reserve used to mitigate demand uncertainty and increased spending needs (e.g., combating fraudulent applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred revenue estimation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate deferred revenue by analyzing the process for completing each fee service and applying the percent incomplete—based on inventory of pending work and completion status—to fee collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferred revenue is largely impacted by changes in filings, first action pendency, and fee rates; unearned patent fees made up the majority of deferred revenue in FY2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark first action pendency targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust first action pendency targets for Trademarks to specified ranges: between 2.5 and 4.5 months in FY2021 and between 2.5 and 6.0 months in FY2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets reflect backlog and surge management; pendency changes affect deferred revenue and operational planning; USPTO may address oldest-filed applications and consider need for additional examination time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee recognition policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize maintenance fees immediately as earned revenue at the time of payment; maintenance fees for patents are due at 3.5, 7.5, and 11.5 years, with a six‑month window and a six‑month grace period (with surcharge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of maintenance payments (including early payments before fee increases) materially affects earned revenue for a fiscal year; late payments/lapses require petition and fees for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and internal control expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieve an unmodified (clean) audit opinion on financial statements, report no material weaknesses or significant deficiencies in internal controls, and resolve previously identified significant deficiencies (e.g., IT security).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KPMG LLP issued an unmodified opinion for FY2021 and reported no material weaknesses or significant deficiencies; continuous improvement and remediation of identified issues are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic invoicing and Vendor Portal adoption (OMB M-15-19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition to electronic invoicing for appropriate federal procurements and implement a Vendor Portal to facilitate invoicing and vendor interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO selected an electronic invoicing solution by end of FY2018, began vendor adoption in FY2019, and increased Vendor Portal usage in FY2021 (added 76 new vendors, a >304% increase); Vendor Portal supports payments, contract status, deliverables submission, direct solicitations, and offers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Analytics product use and culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage Enterprise Data Warehouse (structured data) and Big Data Reservoir (unstructured data), use business intelligence and ETL tools, and shift toward viewing data as an asset to support financial management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EDW users employ Business Objects and Tableau; system admins use SAP Data Services; expanded data analytics (e.g., Alteryx) will support workload forecasting and automated business models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned revenue recognition timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize fees as earned revenue when the activities to accomplish the work associated with the fee are completed; net income/(cost) for a fiscal year depends on work completed in that year rather than solely on timing of cash collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2021 earned revenue included fees collected in prior years but performed in FY2021, maintenance fees recognized immediately, and fees collected and work performed in FY2021; maintenance fees significantly affect matching of costs and revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating reserves usage policy and typical reliance timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use operating reserves to level operations when fee collections are partially/wholly unavailable, lower than expected, when demand unexpectedly increases, or when other unanticipated spending is necessary to maintain operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating reserves are typically relied upon more heavily at the beginning of a fiscal year due to continuing resolutions, reprogramming lags, and start‑of‑year obligations; reserves provide immediate liquidity as fee collections build.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTFRF deposits and reprogramming requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit incremental fee collections that exceed appropriation levels into the Patent and Trademark Fee Reserve Fund (PTFRF); these deposits require Congressional reprogramming to be made available for spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: early patent fee collections were deposited in PTFRF and a $231.9 million reprogramming request was later approved (March 1, 2021) to make funds available to finance operations.
